test_name: Infectious Mononucleosis Profile by IFA - Serum
page_title: Mononucleosis (Mono) Test - Price, Range and Preparation | Metropolis Healthcare

faqs.question: What does Infectious Mononucleosis Profile measure?
faqs.answer: This test detects the presence of Infectious Mononucleosis (IM) heterophile antibodies in your blood, which are produced in response to the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV).

faqs.question: Why is Infectious Mononucleosis Profile done?
faqs.answer: • To detect IM heterophile antibodies in serum • To confirm a suspected diagnosis of infectious mononucleosis • To assess the stage of the infection • To monitor the effectiveness of treatment • To rule out other conditions that have similar symptoms

faqs.question: When is Infectious Mononucleosis Profile recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: Your doctor might recommend this test if you have • symptoms suggestive of infectious mononucleosis such as fever, sore throat, swollen lymph nodes, and fatigue, • suspected exposure to EBV, • complications suggestive of infectious mononucleosis such as enlargement of the spleen or liver, or • immunosuppression or a weakened immune system.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Infectious Mononucleosis Profile are abnormal?
faqs.answer: An elevated level of heterophile antibodies indicates the presence of EBV infection leading to infectious mononucleosis.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Infectious Mononucleosis Profile - Serum?
faqs.answer: This test requires a blood sample to be drawn from your arm. The sample will be then sent to a laboratory for testing.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Infectious Mononucleosis Profile?
faqs.answer: • Inform your healthcare provider of any medications that you are taking. • Avoid certain medications before the test because they can interfere with the results. • Inform your doctor if you have any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with Infectious Mononucleosis Profile?
faqs.answer: • Complete blood count (CBC) to measure white blood cells count • Liver function tests (LFTs) to assess liver function • EBV DNA polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test to detect EBV DNA.

faqs.question: What is Infectious Mononucleosis Profile also known as?
faqs.answer: Heterophile Antibody Test or Rapid Mono Test

faqs.question: What is infectious mononucleosis?
faqs.answer: Infectious mononucleosis is a viral infection caused by EBV. It spreads through saliva and close contact with an infected person. Symptoms include fever, sore throat, fatigue, swollen lymph nodes, and enlarged spleen or liver.
